ops.text: The codex-wrapper agent pattern orphaned or lost track of its codex process three times in one day on the rm-guard work: (1) the implementer backgrounded codex-ask with an `until [ -s reply ]` poll loop, codex died silently mid-run (log just stops after an item.started, no turn.completed), and the wrapper reported "still actively running" off the stale log; (2+3) both reviewer wrappers armed process-exit Monitors, went idle, and the Monitors never fired — the completed reply files (non-empty, timestamps 12:04/12:12) sat unread for ~5 hours until the orchestrator recovered them from /var/folders/.../codex-ask.*/codex-r-* directly. Liveness must be judged by the process tree (ps), completion by a non-empty reply file, and the wrapper needs to survive its own Monitor dying — or codex-ask should write a terminal sentinel (exit status line) into the reply file even on failure so pollers can distinguish dead from slow.
